'''Newport''' is a {{convert|600|acre|km2|1|adj=on}} master-planned, [[mixed-use development|mixed-use]] community in [[Downtown Jersey City]], in the [[U.S. state]] of [[New Jersey]], consisting of retail, residential, office, and entertainment facilities.  The neighborhood is situated on the [[Hudson Waterfront]].  Prior to development, the area was home to the [[Erie Railroad]]'s [[Pavonia Terminal]].  The area is located opposite [[Lower Manhattan]] and the [[Tribeca]] neighborhood in [[New York City]].  Redevelopment of Newport began in 1986 as a $10 billion project led by real-estate tycoon [[Samuel J. LeFrak]] and his firm The LeFrak Organization.<ref>{{cite news |author=Weiss, Lois |date=August 27, 1997 |title=Newport dream becoming reality - developer Samuel LeFrak's planned Newport community in New Jersey |url=http://www.findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_m3601/is_n4_v44/ai_19953443 |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120315122848/https://www.findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_m3601/is_n4_v44/ai_19953443 |archive-date=March 15, 2012 |issue=4 |volume=44 |access-date=June 12, 2024 |publisher=Real Estate Weekly}}</ref><ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.nytimes.com/2012/05/01/nyregion/for-newport-in-jersey-city-last-phase-of-development-begins.html | work=The New York Times | first=Charles V. | last=Bagli | title=For Newport in Jersey City, Last Phase of Development Begins | date=April 30, 2012}}</ref>

==History==
Newport's name was changed from "Newport City" to just "Newport" in 1988.<ref>{{cite web |title=Newport Redevelopment Plan |url=https://www.cityofjerseycity.com/UserFiles/Servers/Server_6189660/File/I%20Want%20To/Get%20Information/Redevelopment%20Plans/60%20Newport.pdf |website=City of Jersey City |publisher=City of Jersey City |access-date=9 December 2020 |pages=1 }}</ref>

==Transportation==
[[NJ Transit|New Jersey Transit]]'s [[Hudson-Bergen Light Rail]]'s [[Newport station (Hudson–Bergen Light Rail)|Newport station]] and [[Port Authority Trans-Hudson]]'s ("PATH") [[Newport station (PATH)|Newport station]] are located in Newport. The area is also served by several New Jersey Transit bus lines, as well as other private bus lines. [[Interstate 78 in New Jersey|Interstate 78]] is nearby and connects to the [[Holland Tunnel]], which provides vehicle access to [[Lower Manhattan]], as well as to the [[New Jersey Turnpike]].

==Land use==
===Retail shopping and dining===
[[File:Newport Jersey City November 2021 003.jpg|thumb|left|Aerial view of the Newport Centre Mall]]
Part of the Newport community is the [[Newport Centre Mall]], a large traditional indoor shopping complex anchored by [[Macy's]], [[JCPenney]], [[Kohl's]], [[H&M]], [[Dick's Sporting Goods]], and [[Zara (retailer)|ZARA]].  Outside the mall and around the Newport area are a variety of primarily neighborhood oriented restaurants (known collectively as "The Restaurants at Newport") and retail stores<ref>{{cite news|title=How Far to the Organic Arugula?|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|author=Martin, Antoinette |date=August 5, 2007 | url=https://www.nytimes.com/2007/08/05/realestate/05njzo.html?ex=1343966400&en=fa97d6119138cb06&ei=5088&partner=rssnyt&emc=rss}}</ref> (known collectively as "The Newport River Market").  This includes a number of notables such as a [[Target Corporation|Target]] store which opened in 2004,<ref>{{cite news|title=Target plans opening near NYC: Greatland would be most accessible for Manhattanites |publisher=DSN Retailing Today |author=Scardino, Emily |date=April 7, 2003 | url=http://www.findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_m0FNP/is_7_42/ai_99982372| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090530193704/http://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_m0FNP/is_7_42/ai_99982372/| url-status=usurped|issue=7 |volume=42 | archive-date=May 30, 2009}}</ref> and [[Best Buy]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Best Buy in Newport, Jersey City|url=http://www.destinationjerseycity.com/vendors/best-buy/|work=destinationjerseycity.com}}</ref>

===Housing===
As of 2014, the population of Newport is 15,000.<ref name="UnionCityReporter">"Newport section of JC has it all". "Home". ''[[The Union City Reporter]]''. June 8, 2014. p. 3.</ref> Newport's approved master Redevelopment Plan contains an 'as-of-right' entitlement to build 9,000 units of residential housing.  Newport currently includes 10 high-rise rental apartment buildings comprising approximately 4,000 households.  Construction of these buildings began in 1985.  Newport's 10th rental apartment building, "The Aquablu," was completed and occupied in 2009.  Newport also includes 3 high-rise condominium apartment buildings comprising approximately 900 additional households.  Construction of these condominium buildings began in 1987.  The most recent condominium building, known as "The Shore Condominiums at Newport, North Tower" was completed in 2008.  Several adjacent residential buildings just south of Thomas Gangemi Drive along the 10th Street embankment are outside of the Newport Redevelopment Zone,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cityofjerseycity.com/UserFiles/Servers/Server_6189660/File/I%20Want%20To/Get%20Information/Redevelopment%20Plans/60%20Newport.pdf|title=Newport Redevelopment Plan|publisher=City of Jersey City}}</ref> but because they are developed by the LeFrak organization,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://jerseydigs.com/lefraks-embankment-house-at-715-jersey-ave/|title=Lefrak's Embankment House at 715 Jersey Ave|last=Digs|first=Jersey|date=2015-11-09|website=Jersey Digs|language=en-US|access-date=2019-04-28}}</ref> are often advertised by real estate professionals as being in Newport.{{citation needed|date=June 2014}}

Many buildings offer views of the [[North River (Hudson River)|Hudson River]] and the [[New York City skyline]].  A portion of the [[Hudson River Waterfront Walkway]] runs through Newport.

===Hotels===
Newport's approved master Redevelopment Plan contains an 'as-of-right' entitlement to build 1,200 hotel rooms.  A 187-room hotel known as the [[Courtyard by Marriott]] Jersey City-Newport opened south of Newport in 2000.  A 429-room full-service hotel known as the [[Westin Hotels & Resorts|Westin]] Newport, Jersey City opened in 2009.<ref>{{cite news|title=Mayor: High hopes for Newport hotel |publisher=The Jersey Journal |author=Clark, Amy Sara |date=January 28, 2009 | url=http://www.nj.com/news/jjournal/jerseycity/index.ssf?/base/news-7/1233127532204150.xml&coll=3}}</ref>

===Office buildings===
The "Newport Office Center" consists of 8 buildings which in total amount to over {{convert|5000000|sqft|m2}} of Class A commercial office space.  The first of these buildings, 111 Town Square Place, was built from the remnants of an abandoned warehouse in 1989.  It contains both office and data centers.  The most recent building, 100 Town Square Place was completed in 2003.  Hundreds of different companies have headquarters or back-offices at Newport.  These range from transportation companies such as [[EVA Air]]<ref>"[http://www.evaair.com/html/b2c/english/club/SERVICE_CENTER Service Center] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090204183738/http://evaair.com/html/b2c/english/club/service_center |date=2009-02-04 }}." ''[[EVA Air]]''Retrieved on February 7, 2009.</ref> to major financial institutions. The neighborhood’s office towers provide more than six million square feet of office space to major employers including [[JPMorgan Chase|JP Morgan Chase]], [[Citigroup]], [[Fidelity Investments]], [[L'Oréal|L’Oreal]], [[Forbes]], and [[Tory Burch LLC|Tory Burch]].  Furthermore, it houses more than 25,000 employees.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://njbiz.com/ny-waterway-ferry-resume-service-newport/|title = NY Waterway ferry to resume service at Newport|last = Lindner|first = Linda|date = 28 January 2019|website = NJBIZ}}</ref> In March 2019, the LeFrak Organization sold the 350,000 square foot office tower, 570 Washington Boulevard, for $170 million.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://therealdeal.com/2019/03/12/new-jersey-cheat-sheet-jersey-city-office-tower-sells-for-170m-mack-cali-buys-metropark-building-amid-big-portfolio-sale-more/|title=New Jersey Cheat Sheet: Jersey City office tower sells for $170M, Mack-Cali buys Metropark building amid big portfolio sale… & more|last=Klatell|first=James|date=2019-03-12|website=The Real Deal New York|language=en-US|access-date=2019-04-23}}</ref>

==Newport 10,000==
The Newport 10,000, more popularly known as the ''Newport 10k'', is a 10 kilometer road race (running) in the vicinity of the [[Hudson River Waterfront Walkway]].<ref>Steadman, Andrew (May 14, 2012). [http://www.nj.com/jjournal-news/index.ssf/2012/05/some_1300_runners_participate.html "Some 1,300 runners participate in Newport 10K race, largest turnout ever"]. [[NJ.com]].</ref> Typically held the second weekend in May, the race tends to attract a strong regional and international field of elite runners. The course is [[USATF]] certified and consists of flat local roads.<ref>{{cite web| title=Website newport10k.com |url=http://www.newport10k.com/|work=website|publisher=www.OYMP.net|access-date=16 May 2012}}</ref>
